t.6.44.1: Seeing that very great deed performed by the foremost of the monkeys, Akampana summoned up fierce wrath in the battle.
t.6.44.2: His form overwhelmed with rage, shaking his supreme bow, he beheld the deeds of his enemies and spoke these words to his charioteer.
t.6.44.3: Charioteer, drive the chariot swiftly to that very spot at once! There these many are slaying a great many rākṣasas in battle.
t.6.44.4: Here indeed stand these mighty monkeys of fearsome bodies, armed with trees and rocks as their weapons, before my very face.
t.6.44.5: For I wish to slay these who boast of battle; by them the entire rākṣasa army is seen to be crushed.
t.6.44.6: Then Akampana, foremost among chariot-warriors, in his chariot drawn by swift horses, struck the monkeys in anger with volleys of arrows.
t.6.44.7: The monkeys could not even stand their ground in the battle, much less fight; broken by the arrows of Akampana, all of them fled.
t.6.44.8: Seeing his kinsmen fallen into the power of death, overcome by Akampana, the mighty Hanumān came to their aid.
t.6.44.9: Seeing that great monkey, all the heroic leaders of the monkey troops came together in the battle and, united, surrounded him.
t.6.44.10: Seeing Hanūmān standing firm, those leaders of the monkey troops became strong, for they had taken refuge in one who was strong.
t.6.44.11: But Akampana showered arrows upon Hanūmān, who stood firm like a mountain, as great Indra pours down torrents of rain.
t.6.44.12: Disregarding the floods of sharp arrows that had fallen upon his body, the mighty one set his mind on the slaying of Akampana.
t.6.44.13: Laughing aloud, the greatly splendid Hanumān, son of the Wind-god, rushed at that rākṣasa, as though making the earth tremble.
t.6.44.14: As he roared aloud, blazing with his fiery energy, his form became unassailable, like that of a blazing fire.
t.6.44.15: But knowing himself to be without a weapon, the bull among monkeys, filled with rage, swiftly uprooted a mountain.
t.6.44.16: Seizing that great mountain-rock with one hand, the mighty Māruti let out a tremendous roar and whirled it about.
t.6.44.17: Then he rushed upon Akampana, that lord of the Rākṣasas, just as Puraṃdara, with his thunderbolt, rushed upon Namuci in battle.
t.6.44.18: But Akampana, seeing that mountain peak raised aloft, shattered it from afar with great crescent-headed arrows.
t.6.44.19: Seeing that mountain peak, split apart in the sky by the arrows of the rākṣasa, fall scattered in pieces, Hanūmān was overcome with rage.
t.6.44.20: Filled with rage and pride, that monkey approached an aśvakarṇa tree and swiftly uprooted it, towering like a great mountain.
t.6.44.21: Seizing that aśvakarṇa tree with its massive trunk, the one of great splendor laughed and, with the greatest delight, whirled it about in the battle.
t.6.44.22: Running forward with great speed and forcefully shattering the trees, Hanūmān, supremely enraged, split the earth with his feet.
t.6.44.23: The wise Hanumān slew the elephants together with their riders, the chariot-warriors together with their chariots, and the rākṣasas fighting on foot.
t.6.44.24: Seeing Hanūmān, enraged like Antaka, the Ender, taking lives in battle, the Rākṣasas fled in all directions.
t.6.44.25: The heroic Akampana saw him rushing upon him, enraged, bringing terror to the Rākṣasas, and he grew angry and roared.
t.6.44.26: With fourteen sharp arrows that rend the body, Akampana pierced Hanūmān of great valor.
t.6.44.28: Then, uprooting another tree and putting forth unsurpassed force, he swiftly struck Akampana, the lord of the rākṣasas, on the head.
t.6.44.27: Pierced thus by many showers of arrows, the heroic Hanumān appeared like a mountain overgrown with vegetation.
t.6.44.29: Struck with a tree by that great-souled lord of the monkeys, who was filled with anger, the rākṣasa fell down and died.
t.6.44.30: Seeing Akampana, that lord of the rākṣasas, struck down upon the ground, all the rākṣasas were shaken, like trees in an earthquake.
t.6.44.31: Having cast away their weapons, all those defeated rākṣasas, terrified and pursued by those vānaras, fled toward Laṅkā.
t.6.44.32: With their hair hanging loose, bewildered, their pride shattered and defeated, they fled in all directions, panting, their limbs streaming with the sweat of exhaustion.
t.6.44.33: Crushing one another, they entered the city out of fear, utterly bewildered and looking behind them again and again.
t.6.44.34: When those rākṣasas had entered Laṅkā, all the mighty monkeys came together and honored Hanūmān.
t.6.44.35: And Hanūmān too, endowed with courage and delighted, honored all those monkeys in return, each as he deserved and with kindness.
t.6.44.36: The monkeys, flushed with victory, roared with all their might, and there they dragged the rākṣasas about again while they were still alive.
t.6.44.38: Then the hosts of gods honored the monkey, and so did Rāma himself and the exceedingly mighty Lakṣmaṇa; likewise the monkeys headed by Sugrīva, and the greatly powerful Vibhīṣaṇa too, honored him then.
t.6.44.37: Having closed with the rākṣasas and slain them, the great monkey Māruti attained the glory of a hero, just as Viṣṇu did when, at the head of the army, he slew the mighty one, the terrible great asura, destroyer of his foes.
